The DOM elements serve as the sole source of truth for state.

The outer wrapper is a CSS grid with two equal 1fr columns and a 20px gap. The grid defines four named areas: the left column is a single area spanning all row tracks; the right column is split into three row areas stacked top to bottom — nav, media, caption.

### Goal

Build an editorial photo stack component that displays a vertically centred column of images with captions on desktop, and switches to a full-width drag-and-swipe slider with dot pagination on mobile. web-text/AsymmetricTwoColArticleLayout.h:
### Goal

A journal/editorial article listing component that renders an asymmetric two-column grid on desktop and a full-width autoplay carousel on mobile. A shared data array drives both views from a single source. The component displays a section heading, a featured large article on the left, two smaller articles stacked on the right, and a centred "Discover More" call-to-action link below. Each article entry contains an image, a title, and a short description, and each image is wrapped in an analytics-tagged anchor.

### Dependencies

* Bootstrap 4.6.2 — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@4.6.2/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css
* Splide 4.1.4 CSS — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@splidejs/splide@4.1.4/dist/css/splide.min.css
* Splide 4.1.4 JS — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@splidejs/splide@4.1.4/dist/js/splide.min.js
### Architecture

* The data model is a JavaScript array of entry objects, each holding a desktop image path, a mobile image path, a title, a description, a link URL, and an analytics object with a content ID and content type.
* On DOMContentLoaded, two rendering functions read from this array: one builds the desktop Bootstrap grid by injecting HTML into a container div, the other builds the Splide slide list by injecting <li> elements into the carousel track.
* Both renderers attach the analytics object to each anchor as a JSON-serialised data-content-analytic attribute.
* After the mobile list is built, Splide is initialised on the mobile carousel element.
* The desktop and mobile containers are toggled by Bootstrap's display utilities so only one is visible at a time.
### Layout

* The outer wrapper is centred at 85% of the viewport width.
* **Desktop (768px and above):** A two-column Bootstrap row.
* The left column is 7/12 wide (col-md-7) and holds the featured entry: a full-width image above, then a horizontal row beneath it with the title on the left and the description on the right, side by side using justify-content space-between.
* The right column is 5/12 wide (col-md-5) and holds the remaining entries stacked vertically.
* Each entry in the right column is a row subdivided into a 5/12 image column with no padding and a 7/12 text column; the text column uses flex column layout with space-between to vertically distribute the title and description.
* **Mobile (below 768px):** The desktop grid is hidden.
* A full-width Splide carousel replaces it.
* Each slide contains a portrait image at full width followed by a centred text block (title and description) set at 70% width and centred with auto margins.
* A centred CTA link with top and bottom margin of 3rem (mt-5 mb-5) sits below both views.
### Styling

* Section heading: 30px, font-weight 500, centred, margin 3rem top and 2rem bottom.
* Entry titles: 13px, bold.
* Entry descriptions: 13px, margin-bottom 0.
* All text in the mobile slider is centred.
* Mobile pagination (Splide, mobile carousel):
* Pill shape: 30px wide, 4px tall, border-radius 2px.
* Inactive colour: #ccc. Active colour: #000.
* Horizontal spacing: 8px on each side.
* Positioned 1.5em below the track (bottom: -1.5em).
* Colour transition: 0.3s.
* Desktop carousel pagination (if Splide is also used on desktop):
* Rectangular: 20px wide, 4px tall, border-radius 0, no border, no box-shadow.
* Active colour: #000.
### Behaviour

* Mobile Splide carousel:
* type: loop
* perPage: 1
* autoplay: true
* interval: 4000 ms
* speed: 800 ms
* arrows: false
* pagination: true
* No desktop carousel interaction is defined; the desktop layout is a static grid.
* Each article image and title are wrapped in an anchor.
* Every anchor carries a data-content-analytic attribute containing a JSON object with contentId (string) and contentType (string) for analytics tracking.
* Link href values use a server-side URL template pattern.
### Responsive

* 768px and above: Desktop two-column asymmetric grid is shown; mobile Splide carousel is hidden (d-none d-md-block / d-block d-md-none Bootstrap utilities).
* Below 768px: Desktop grid is hidden; Splide carousel is shown. Section heading reduces to 26px. Each entry renders as a full-width portrait image with centred text block at 70% width below it.
### Code Quality

* All article data is defined in a single array; both the desktop grid and the mobile carousel read from this same array — no duplication of content.
* Desktop and mobile rendering are handled as separate functions, each responsible for injecting its own markup into its own container element.
* Analytics metadata is stored in the data model and serialised to a data-content-analytic attribute at render time, keeping tracking concerns out of the HTML structure.
* The Splide initialisation is guarded by an existence check on the mobile element before mounting.
* Desktop images and mobile images are stored as separate fields per entry, allowing different crops (landscape vs portrait) per breakpoint.

fullwidth/FullWidthVideoWithRedirectOver:
Goal
A full-width video banner that serves two distinct video sources — one for desktop viewports and one for mobile — displayed in a stacked container where only the appropriate video is visible at any given breakpoint. An invisible, full-coverage anchor element is absolutely positioned over the entire video area and carries a redirect URL and content analytics metadata, so that a click anywhere on the banner navigates the user to a target page while logging the interaction. The video plays automatically, loops silently, and fills the container width at all sizes.

Dependencies
No external dependencies.

Architecture
Container: A single relatively-positioned wrapper holds both video elements and the overlay anchor as stacked children.
Video sources: Two separate video elements — desktop (landscape) and mobile (portrait) — each referencing its own MP4 source file.
Visibility toggle: Bootstrap display utility classes (d-none / d-block / d-md-none / d-md-block) control which video renders at each breakpoint. No JavaScript is required for this switch.
Overlay anchor: An absolutely-positioned anchor stretches to 100% width and height of the container at z-index 2, carrying the redirect href and a data-content-analytic JSON attribute for analytics tracking.

Layout
* The wrapper is a block element spanning the full available width with position: relative and no fixed height — height is driven entirely by the video's natural aspect ratio.
* Both video elements are set to 100% width with object-fit: cover and height: auto, displayed as block to eliminate inline baseline gaps.
* The overlay anchor sits at absolute position top: 0, left: 0, width: 100%, height: 100%, z-index: 2 with no visible content or text decoration.

Styling
* No background color, border, shadow, or text styling — the component is purely video and an invisible interactive layer.
* The overlay anchor has text-decoration: none and is fully transparent to the eye; its only visual effect is the browser's default pointer cursor on hover.
* No transitions or animations beyond the video's own playback.

Behaviour
Autoplay: Both videos carry autoplay, muted, loop, and playsinline attributes so they begin playing immediately on page load without sound, looping indefinitely, and playing inline on iOS rather than fullscreen.
Controls: Native browser video controls are present but sit below z-index 2, so the overlay intercepts all pointer events and the controls are effectively unreachable by clicking.
Click redirect: A click anywhere on the banner follows the anchor's href, which is a dynamic SFCC template expression resolving to a category or content page URL.
Analytics: The overlay anchor carries a data-content-analytic attribute containing a JSON object with keys: contentId, contentType, itemId, link, and text. Values identify the banner placement and asset for downstream event tracking.

Responsive
* < md (768px): Desktop video hidden. Mobile portrait video shown. Banner height is driven by the portrait video's aspect ratio.
* >= md (768px): Mobile video hidden. Desktop landscape video shown. Banner height is driven by the landscape video's aspect ratio. Both overlay and analytics attribute remain identical across breakpoints.

### Goal

A full-width horizontal image and video carousel that loops continuously and supports free-drag scrolling. Slides are rendered dynamically from a JavaScript data array, each optionally wrapping its media in an anchor link and displaying an optional text overlay. * Active state: #000000 fill at full opacity.
* No scale transform on the active dot.

### Goal

Build a full-width hero banner carousel with separate slide sets for desktop and mobile. Each slide displays a full-bleed image or autoplaying video with a text overlay pinned to the bottom-left of the slide. The slider uses a crossfade transition between slides, autoplays continuously, and displays bar-style pagination dots in the bottom-right corner. Both the active pagination dot colour and the per-slide autoplay interval are driven by per-slide data, updating dynamically as the carousel advances.

### Dependencies

* Splide @splidejs/splide@4.1.4 (CSS + JS via CDN). Bootstrap @4.6.2 (CSS only, for responsive display utilities).
### Architecture

* Slide content is stored in two separate JavaScript arrays — one for desktop slides, one for mobile slides — each containing objects with fields for title text, discover link text, text colour, pagination dot colour, link URL or tab-link destination, analytics attributes, media source and type, and autoplay interval in milliseconds.
* A shared slide-builder function generates the inner HTML for each slide from a data object, producing a linked wrapper containing the media element and the overlay text.
* A separate render function iterates over a data array, creates list items with per-slide data attributes for autoplay timer and pagination colour, calls the builder, and appends them to a target Splide list element.

* Desktop and mobile sliders are initialised independently after both slide lists have been rendered.
* A separate DOMContentLoaded handler resolves tab-link hrefs at runtime by reading the country-code segment from the URL pathname and constructing the target URL with a hash-based tab parameter.
### Layout

* A single full-viewport-width container holds two Splide carousels stacked in the same position — the desktop carousel is hidden on screens narrower than the Bootstrap md breakpoint (768px), the mobile carousel is hidden at md and above.
* Each slide fills the full width of its carousel.
* The media element fills the slide at 100% width and height with object-fit: cover.
* The text overlay is positioned absolutely, pinned 20px from the bottom and 20px from the left edge of each slide.
### Styling

* Navigation arrows are hidden.
* Pagination sits at the bottom-right of the slider: 20px from the bottom, 2.5rem from the right edge, with a 7px gap between dots.
* Each pagination dot is a flat bar — 28px wide, 4px tall, zero border-radius, background rgba(128,128,128,0.5).
* The active dot grows to 6px tall; its background colour switches between #ffffff and #000000 based on a data-pagination-color attribute (white or black) on the slider root element.
* All dot transitions use a 0.3s ease transition.
* The overlay title is 22px, weight 600, line-height 1.2.

* Splide is configured with type: 'fade', rewind: true, speed: 800, arrows: false, pagination: true, autoplay: true, pauseOnHover: false, pauseOnFocus: false.

* On the moved event, the interval is updated to the incoming slide's autoplay timer value.

* Analytics metadata is embedded as a data-content-analytic JSON attribute on each slide's anchor.
* Video slides autoplay, mute, loop, and use playsinline.
### Responsive

* Below 768px (Bootstrap md): the desktop slider is hidden, the mobile slider is shown.
* The mobile slider uses a separate portrait-oriented image set.
* No changes to text sizes, overlay position, or pagination layout between breakpoints — the two sliders are entirely separate instances with different image assets suited to each form factor.

* All slide content is defined in plain data arrays at the top of the script — no markup is hand-authored for individual slides.

### Goal

A horizontally centred tab navigation bar that controls the visibility of multiple content panels below it. Clicking a tab makes the corresponding panel visible while hiding all others. The active tab is visually distinguished and the first tab and its panel are active by default on load.

### Dependencies

* No external dependencies.
### Architecture

* Each tab link carries a data attribute that maps to the id of its corresponding panel.
* On click, the script removes the active state from all tabs and all panels, then applies the active state to the clicked tab and the panel whose id matches the tab's data attribute.
* Tabs and panels are fully decoupled from each other except through this id-to-data-attribute mapping.
### Layout

* The navigation is a single horizontal row of tab links centred on the page, with 32px gaps between each link.
* A 1px bottom border runs the full width of the nav row, sitting flush against the bottom edge of the links.
* Below the nav row there is 32px of space before the panel area.
* Each panel occupies the full content width.
### Styling

* Nav link: proxima-nova, 13px, weight 500, letter-spacing 0.08em, uppercase, 12px bottom padding, default colour #999, transitions to #000 on active state over 0.2s
* Active indicator: a 1px tall, full-width #000 underline pseudo-element anchored to the bottom of each link; it scales in from scaleX(0) to scaleX(1) with transform-origin left over 0.25s ease when the link becomes active, and reverses when deactivated
* Panels: hidden by default (display none), shown (display block) when active
* Panel content image: full-width block image
* Panel content text: proxima-nova, 14px, centred, 20px padding on all sides
### Behaviour

* Clicking a tab link:
* Removes the active class from all tab links
* Removes the active class from all panels
* Adds the active class to the clicked link, triggering the colour change to #000 and the underline scale-in animation
* Adds the active class to the panel whose id matches the clicked link's data attribute, making it visible
### Responsive

* No breakpoint-specific changes.

* The page is a vertical stack of independent scroll sections with no gaps.
* Each section has an explicit total scroll height that determines how long the zoom animation plays: Section 1 is 250vh, Section 2 is 400vh, Section 3 is 300vh, Section 4 is 500vh.
* Inside every section, a sticky container locks to the top of the viewport and fills it entirely (100vh tall, horizontally centred, overflow hidden).
* Within the sticky container, the image container is centred both horizontally and vertically using flex.
* A floating label is absolutely positioned near the top-centre of the sticky area.
### Styling

* The image container has a fixed pixel size per section: Section 1 is 300×400px (portrait), Section 2 is 600×400px (landscape), Section 3 is 400×400px (square), Section 4 is 250×450px (tall portrait).
* The image inside fills the container fully using object-fit cover.
* The image has a base border-radius of 8px that animates to 0px as zoom-in progresses, or from 0px back to 8px as zoom-out progresses.
* The scale transform uses a 0.1s ease-out CSS transition on top of the JS-driven value to smooth rapid scroll events.
* The section label is a pill badge absolutely positioned 40px from the top, horizontally centred; it has a dark semi-transparent background (rgba 0,0,0,0.5), backdrop blur of 10px, 20px border-radius, 16px font size, 8px vertical and 18px horizontal padding, and 0.7 opacity.
### Behaviour

* On scroll and on resize, each section recalculates its progress independently.
* Progress is 0 when the section top is still below the viewport, 1 when the section bottom has scrolled above the viewport bottom, and a linear ratio of pixels scrolled through the scrollable range in between.
* That raw progress is passed through an ease-out cubic function (1 − (1 − x)³).
* For zoom-out sections, the scale starts at the full-coverage value (computed as the maximum of viewport width divided by base image width and viewport height divided by base image height, then multiplied by the section's zoomOverflow factor) and decreases linearly toward 1 as progress moves from 0 to 1.
* Section 1 uses zoomOverflow 1.1; Section 3 uses zoomOverflow 1.05.
* For zoom-in sections, the scale starts at 1 and increases toward the full-coverage value as progress moves from 0 to 1.
* Section 2 uses zoomOverflow 1.2; Section 4 uses zoomOverflow 1.3.
* The full-coverage scale recalculates on every resize event so the effect remains correct at any viewport size.
### Responsive

* There are no explicit breakpoints.
* The component is inherently responsive because the full-coverage scale is recomputed dynamically from the live viewport dimensions on every scroll and resize event.
* The image containers retain their fixed pixel dimensions at all viewport sizes; only the computed scale changes to always fill the viewport.

special/textleft-rightimgscroll.html:
A two-panel editorial layout where the left panel stays fixed in the viewport while the user scrolls through a vertical stack of images on the right. As the user scrolls, the image closest to the vertical centre of the screen is considered active: it receives a visible outline, the corresponding list item in the left panel becomes bold and highlighted, and all images are scaled relative to their distance from the viewport centre using a cosine curve. Hovering a list item in the left panel smoothly scrolls the right panel to bring the matching image into view. The overall effect is a guided lookbook experience where navigation state is always synchronised between the two panels.

### Dependencies

* No external dependencies.
### Architecture

* The data model is a flat list of items, each pairing a label string with an image source.
* Both the left-panel list items and the right-panel image containers are rendered from this list, with each pair linked by a shared identifier (a data-target attribute on list items, matching id on image containers).
* Two event listeners drive the component: a scroll listener and a resize listener, both calling the same active-state update function on every event.
* That function iterates all images, computes each image's distance from the viewport vertical centre, applies a cosine-derived scale transform, identifies the closest image, and then assigns an active class to the corresponding image container and list item simultaneously — clearing all others first.
* A separate mouseenter listener on each list item triggers a smooth scroll to its paired image container, but does not directly set active state; active state is always resolved by the scroll/resize handler.
### Layout

* Horizontal flex row at the outermost level, offset by a configurable CSS variable (--header-height, default 0px).
* Left panel is 35% wide, sticky, pinned to the top, and exactly calc(100vh - var(--header-height)) tall — it never scrolls.
* Its content is centred both vertically and horizontally via a column flex layout with padding 60px 40px.
* Right panel is 65% wide with padding 40px on all sides; it scrolls naturally with the page.
* Each image sits inside its own container that is 50vh tall with 40px vertical margins, centred both axes.
* Images render at 50% of their container width.
### Styling

* Left panel:
* Background #111, white text, padding 60px 40px
* Heading 32px, margin-bottom 30px
* List items 18px, default opacity 0.6, no list markers, cursor pointer, margin-bottom 16px
* Hover and active states: opacity 1, translate right 6px, transition opacity 0.3s, transform 0.3s
* Active state additionally sets font-weight 600 and color #fff
* Right panel:
* Background #f5f5f5
* Image border-radius 10px, box-shadow 0 5px 15px rgba(0,0,0,0.2), max-width 100%
* Image scale transform transitions at 0.2s
* Active image container gains outline 3px solid #000, outline transitions at 0.3s
* Scale effect: scale = max(0.5, cos(distance / halfViewport × π/2)) — images near the centre approach 1.0; images far from centre approach 0.5
### Behaviour

* **On hover (list item):** smoothly scrolls the page so the linked image container reaches the centre of the viewport using scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center' }).
* **On scroll / resize:** recalculates all image scales and active states.
* The image whose centre is geometrically closest to window.innerHeight / 2 receives the active class; its paired list item also receives the active class.
* All other active classes are cleared before reassigning.
* **On load:** the update function runs once immediately to set initial scale and active states without waiting for a scroll event.
* Active state is determined solely by proximity, not by which item was last hovered — hovering triggers scroll, and scroll triggers state update.

* ≤ 768px — layout switches to a single column (flex-direction: column). Left panel becomes width: 100%, loses sticky positioning (position: relative, top: 0), height becomes auto. Right panel becomes width: 100% with reduced padding 20px. Image containers become width: 100vw, auto height, zero margin.
### Code Quality

* All items — list entries and image containers — are rendered from a single data array; adding or removing a look requires only editing the data, not the rendering logic.
* The active-state logic is contained in one function called by both scroll and resize listeners, and once on init — no state is duplicated between event handlers.
* The hover-to-scroll function and the scale/active-state function are kept separate so they can be extended independently.
* The CSS custom property --header-height (default 0px) is used in both the sticky top offset and the layout margin-top, so integrating a real site header requires changing one value only.

### Goal

A fixed overlay text element is centered on screen and persists while the user scrolls through a page. As different content sections enter the viewport, the overlay text updates to show two adjacent text spans — one in a heavier weight and one in a lighter weight — with independently configurable colors per section. When the final section of the page enters view, the overlay transitions from a fixed viewport position to an absolutely positioned element anchored within that final section, ensuring it scrolls away naturally with the page rather than floating over content below.

### Dependencies

* Bootstrap 4.6.2 — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@4.6.2/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css
### Architecture

* Each content section carries its own text and color configuration as data attributes directly on the element (data-text1, data-text2, data-color1, data-color2).
* A single IntersectionObserver watches all trigger sections.
* When a section crosses the 70% visibility threshold, it reads its own data attributes and injects the text into the overlay.
* The overlay element itself is a single DOM node that is re-parented between the document body (for fixed positioning) and the final section container (for absolute positioning) depending on which section is active.
* There is no external state object — the data attributes are the source of truth.
### Layout

* The overlay text container is centered both horizontally and vertically using fixed positioning with left: 50%, top: 50%, and a transform of -50%, -50% on both axes.
* It sits above all page content at z-index 50.
* The two text spans are displayed inline, side by side, separated by three non-breaking spaces.
* The page wrapper has position: relative to serve as the containing block when the overlay is re-parented into the final section.
### Styling

* **Overlay font size:** 20px
* **Heavy span (first word/phrase):** aktiv-grotesk-extended, weight 500
* **Light span (second word/phrase):** aktiv-grotesk-extended, weight 300
* **Span colors:** set inline per section via data attributes; each span has its own independent color
* **Pointer events:** none on the overlay container so it does not block click interactions beneath it
* **Final section:** overflow: hidden and position: relative to correctly contain the absolutely positioned overlay when re-parented
* No animations or transitions on the text change itself — the update is immediate
### Behaviour

* When any trigger section reaches 70% intersection with the viewport, the overlay text is replaced with the section's data-text1 (heavy span) and data-text2 (light span), each colored by data-color1 and data-color2 respectively.
* If the intersecting section is the final section of the page, the overlay's positioning switches from fixed (viewport-relative) to absolute and the overlay node is moved inside the final section container, so it scrolls with that section.
* When the final section exits the viewport (user scrolls back up), the overlay is moved back to the document body and reverts to fixed positioning, resuming its viewport-centered behavior.
* The IntersectionObserver threshold is **0.7** (70% of the section must be visible before the update fires).
* The desktop overlay is shown only at lg breakpoint and above using Bootstrap's d-none d-lg-block utility.
* A mobile overlay variant is present in the markup but commented out.
### Responsive

* **Below lg (< 992px):** The desktop overlay is hidden (d-none). No overlay text is displayed. The mobile overlay slot exists in the markup but is commented out and not rendered.
* **lg and above (≥ 992px):** The desktop overlay is visible (d-lg-block) and the full scroll-trigger behavior is active.

A centered text label is fixed to the viewport at all times, sitting horizontally and vertically centered over all page content. As the user scrolls, designated trigger sections enter the viewport and cause the sticky text to update its content and color with a smooth fade-out/fade-in transition. The component has separate desktop and mobile text elements that are shown or hidden via Bootstrap breakpoints, each with slightly different font sizes, while sharing the same content and transition behavior.

* Bootstrap 4.6.2: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@4.6.2/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css
### Architecture
* The page contains a fixed overlay element holding two variants of the sticky text (one for desktop, one for mobile).
* Below that, a series of full-height (or content) trigger sections are laid out in normal document flow.
* An IntersectionObserver watches each trigger section; when a section reaches 60% visibility in the viewport, it fires a text update function that simultaneously fades both sticky elements out, swaps their text content and color, then fades them back in.
* The trigger sections carry their target text and color as data attributes, making the system data-driven and easy to extend.

* The sticky text container is fixed-position, centered horizontally and vertically using left: 50%, top: 50%, and a translate offset of -50% on both axes.

* The desktop variant is hidden below the lg breakpoint; the mobile variant is visible only below lg.
* Trigger sections are standard block-level divs placed sequentially in the document to define scroll zones.

* Desktop size is 20px; mobile size is 15px with a width of 80% (to contain wrapping on narrow screens).

special/quiz-single-hybrid-base.html:
### Goal

Build a multi-step style-quiz tool for a fashion accessories brand. The user answers four sequential questions about their skin tone, lifestyle, colour palette preferences, and dressing style. On completion the quiz either resolves the user's answers into a named style persona (persona mode) or scores each product in the catalogue against the answers and surfaces the highest-scoring matches (score mode). The active mode is controlled by a single configuration constant that can be toggled without touching any other logic. After the quiz, a results screen displays a persona card with a generative canvas background, a curated product grid with staggered fade-up entry animations, a social-sharing action bar, and a PDF download that renders the full results page off-screen and exports it as a multi-page A4 document. The user can restart the quiz at any time and all state resets cleanly.

### Dependencies

* html2canvas 1.4.1 — https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/html2canvas/1.4.1/html2canvas.min.js
* jsPDF 2.5.1 — https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/jspdf/2.5.1/jspdf.umd.min.js
* Google Fonts (Cormorant Garamond: italic and regular at weights 300/400/500; Montserrat at weights 300/400/500/600)
### Architecture

* The question schema is a plain JavaScript array of objects.
* Each object defines a question key, title, subtitle, select mode (single or multi), and an options array.
* Each option carries a display value, name, description, and one of three visual types: a single colour swatch hex, an array of four colour swatch hexes, or an emoji icon.
* The progress bar and all question panels are built dynamically from this schema at page load — no question markup is hand-authored in HTML.
* The product database is a flat array of objects.
* Every product carries two independent tag sets: one set of per-question answer arrays used by score mode, and a personas array used by persona mode.
* Both sets must be populated for every product so either mode works without data changes.
* Two recommendation modes share the same entry point.
* Score mode maps each question's answers to a weighted point value (questions 1 and 2 each worth 3 points, questions 3 and 4 each worth 2 points) and filters products with a score of 4 or higher, falling back to a score of 2 or higher when fewer than four results qualify.
* Persona mode runs a pattern-matching algorithm over the quiz answers using ordered combo strings per persona, where an asterisk matches any value, and returns the first persona whose combo pattern matches — falling back to a catch-all persona.
* A single constant at the top of the script switches between modes.
* The persona canvas background is drawn programmatically using the Canvas 2D API: a linear gradient base using the first two palette colours, five radial soft-circle overlays using the third and fourth palette colours at reduced opacity, and a faint grid of lines for texture.
* No image is required for the background; a product image layered on top falls back to the emoji if the image fails to load.
* Analytics attributes are written as JSON onto the final "view results" button each time the user selects an answer, encoding the full answer combination as a content ID.
* Each product card also carries its own analytics attribute.
### Layout

* The page is a single column centred at 80% width with 24px horizontal padding and 80px bottom padding.
* The header sits above a horizontal progress bar made of alternating step dots (28×28px circles) and connector lines (60px wide, 1px tall) with an animated fill.
* Each question panel occupies the full column width and is hidden until active.
* The options grid uses CSS grid with auto-fill columns, minimum 190px each, and a 16px gap.
* Navigation buttons sit in a space-between flex row below the grid.
* The results screen opens with an optional mode badge, then a horizontal persona card: a fixed 340px visual panel on the left and a flex-1 info panel on the right, separated by no gap (flush).
* Below the persona card is a centred action bar with a label, five social share buttons, a 1px vertical divider, and a filled download button.
* Below that is a results header with filter tags, then a product grid using auto-fill columns at 240px minimum with 24px gap.
### Styling

* CSS custom properties on :root define the full palette: --charcoal #2A2520, --gold #B8962E, --gold-light #D4AF6A, --cream #F5F0E8, --sand #E8DED0, --warm-gray #8C7B6E, --rust #9B4F2A, --sage #6B7B5E, --deep #1A1510.
* The main body font is Montserrat; display headings use Cormorant Garamond.
* The brand name is set at 50px, weight 300, in Cormorant Garamond.
* The tagline is 0.65rem, letter-spacing 0.35em, uppercase.
* Question titles use clamp(1.6rem, 4vw, 2.4rem) at weight 300.
* Question labels are 0.6rem, letter-spacing 0.35em, uppercase, in gold.
* Option card names use Cormorant Garamond at 1.15rem weight 400.
* Option descriptions are 0.68rem with 1.6 line-height.
* Option cards have a 1px sand border, white background, 28px top / 20px side / 22px bottom padding.
* On hover they lift 2px with an 8px/32px box shadow and a gold bottom border animates from 0 to 100% width over 0.3s.
* On selection the card background becomes --charcoal, text becomes --cream or --sand, and a gold check badge (20×20px, top-right 12px) fades in.
* The question panel entrance is a combined opacity-0-to-1 and translateY(18px)-to-0 animation over 0.5s ease.
* Product cards animate in with the same fade-up pattern but staggered at 0.07s per card.
* The persona emoji floats on a 4s ease-in-out loop between translateY(0) and translateY(-10px).
* Navigation buttons: primary uses --charcoal background with --cream text at 0.65rem / letter-spacing 0.25em / uppercase; on hover it shifts right 3px.
* Ghost button has a transparent background with a 1px sand border.
* Both are 14px top/bottom × 36px side padding.
* The download button is the same style as primary.
* Share buttons are 0.6rem / letter-spacing 0.18em / 10px × 20px padding with a 1px sand border; each has a platform-specific hover colour: Facebook #1877F2, Instagram #E1306C, X/Twitter #000, WhatsApp #25D366, Pinterest #E60023.
* A fixed-position toast notification uses a spring cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) to enter from below.
* Product badges: "New In" uses --charcoal background, "On Sale" uses --rust, "Limited Ed." uses --gold.
* All badges are 0.55rem, letter-spacing 0.2em, uppercase, positioned absolute top-left 12px.
* Product images are square (aspect-ratio: 1) with a solid background colour per product.
* Product names use Cormorant Garamond at 1.15rem.
* Product prices are 0.85rem weight 600; the currency symbol is 0.7rem weight 400 in warm-gray.
* The wishlist button is a 30×30px bordered square, no background, that turns rust on hover.
* The persona card info panel has 40px top/bottom × 44px side padding.
* The persona name uses clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3rem) at weight 300; the italic subtitle portion is coloured --gold.
* A 40px × 1px gold divider sits below the name.
* Persona trait pills are 0.58rem, letter-spacing 0.15em, uppercase, with cream background and sand border.
* Mode badges are inline-flex with a preceding bullet character; persona mode uses a sage/green background, score mode uses a warm tan background.
### Behaviour

* Clicking an option card in single-select mode deselects all sibling cards for that question and selects the clicked card.
* In multi-select mode clicking toggles the card's selected state.
* After each selection the Continue/View Results button for the active step is enabled if at least one answer is selected for that question, or disabled if the answer array is empty.
* Clicking Continue advances to the next panel and updates the progress bar — step dots before the active step show a gold filled "done" state with a checkmark (the number text is hidden), the active dot is filled charcoal, future dots are empty.
* The connector line fill animates to 100% width for completed segments.
* Clicking Back returns to the previous panel and regresses the progress bar without clearing the previous answer.
* The final button ("View My Picks") validates that all questions are answered before triggering the results screen; if any question is unanswered an alert is shown.
* On the results screen the persona card resolves immediately.
* The product grid renders with staggered entrance animations.
* The wishlist heart button on each card toggles between an outline and filled heart on click, turning rust when active, without navigating away (event.preventDefault is called).
* Share buttons: Facebook opens a Facebook sharer popup (600×460px) with the page URL and a share text string that includes the persona name, subtitle, and tagline.
* X/Twitter opens a tweet intent popup (600×460px).
* WhatsApp opens the WhatsApp send API in a new tab.
* Pinterest opens the pin creator (750×550px).
* Instagram copies the share text to the clipboard and shows a toast notification.
* All share text is derived from the resolved persona at share time.
* The Download PDF button shows a spinning SVG loader and disables itself during generation.
* It creates a 960px wide off-screen div with inline styles (no stylesheet dependency) containing the brand header, persona card, filter tags, and product grid using emoji instead of images. html2canvas captures this div at scale 2, then jsPDF slices the canvas into A4-height pages and assembles a multi-page PDF.
* The filename is derived from the persona name and subtitle.
* The button restores its original state in a finally block whether the export succeeds or fails.
* Restart clears all answer arrays, removes all selected states, re-enables no navigation buttons, hides the results panel, shows the progress bar, and resets to panel 1.
### Responsive

* At max-width 720px: the persona card switches from a horizontal flex row to a vertical column (flex-direction: column).
* The persona visual panel height reduces from a min-height of 320px to 240px with flex basis 240px.
* The persona info padding reduces from 40px/44px to 28px/24px.
### Code Quality

* All question panels and progress bar segments are rendered from the question schema array — no panel markup is hard-coded in HTML.
* All product cards are rendered from the products array — no card markup is hard-coded.
* The recommendation logic reads from the same product objects regardless of mode; switching modes requires changing only the single RECOMMENDATION_MODE constant.
* The persona resolution algorithm is data-driven: pattern strings in each persona object drive matching without branching logic per persona.
* The PDF export builds its own isolated inline-styled DOM subtree so it is fully independent of the page stylesheet.
* All scoring weights and thresholds are expressed as named values within the scoring function, not scattered magic numbers.
### Output Requirements

* Output in this order: dependency CSS imports, dependency JavaScript imports, HTML, CSS, JavaScript
* Place all dependency imports at the beginning

special/timeline.html:
A full-viewport horizontal timeline that presents an ordered sequence of milestone entries as a side-scrolling narrative. The page scrolls exclusively on the horizontal axis; vertical wheel events are intercepted and remapped to horizontal scrolling so the user never needs a horizontal scrollbar to navigate. Each milestone occupies one full viewport-width panel with its own gradient background. A fixed floating indicator in the bottom-right corner pulses to remind the user that the page scrolls sideways. All section content is rendered dynamically from a JavaScript data array — no milestone HTML exists in the source document.

### Dependencies

* No external dependencies.
### Architecture

* The component has two independent JavaScript systems.
* The first is a data-rendering engine: a single array of objects (one per milestone) drives the creation of all section elements at page load.
* Each object holds the following fields:
* year (number) — four-digit year displayed as the large decorative heading
* date (string) — full human-readable date label (e.g. "January 2020")
* title (string) — short milestone title
* description (string) — one-to-two sentence narrative body text
* badge (string) — short phase label rendered in a pill badge (e.g. "Launch")
* number (string) — zero-padded sequence string used as the watermark ("01"–"07")
* bgColor (string) — CSS gradient string applied as the panel's inline background style
* Iterating the array produces and appends one panel element per entry, including its inline background gradient applied directly as an element style.
* The second system is a scroll remapper: a non-passive wheel listener on window intercepts any event where deltaY is non-zero, calls preventDefault(), and adds that delta directly to the document body's scrollLeft.
* The two systems are fully independent — rendering runs once at load, the scroll remapper runs continuously during user interaction.
### Layout

* The outermost wrapper is a horizontal flex row sized to max-content width, containing a purely decorative horizontal rule positioned at vertical centre (absolute, full width) and the dynamically generated panels stacked side-by-side.
* Each panel is 100vw wide and 100vh tall, centred both axes, with 100px left and right padding.
* The body scrolls only horizontally (overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden).
* Inside each panel a content card is layered above the timeline rule via z-index.
* A large watermark number sits in the top-left corner of each panel behind the card.
* The scroll hint badge is fixed in the viewport bottom-right at 30px from each edge.
* Exact values: panel width 100vw, panel height 100vh, panel padding 0 100px, content card max-width 600px, timeline rule height 3px, scroll hint fixed 30px from bottom and right edges.
### Styling

* The page background (visible during load and in the scrollbar track area) is #0f0c29.
* The horizontal timeline rule is a three-stop linear gradient: #667eea → #764ba2 (at 50%) → #f093fb.
* The custom scrollbar thumb repeats this gradient horizontally; the track is #1a1a2e; scrollbar height is 12px with 10px border-radius on the thumb.
* Each panel has a unique 135° two-stop gradient background applied in sequence order:
* #667eea → #764ba2
* #f093fb → #f5576c
* #4facfe → #00f2fe
* #43e97b → #38f9d7
* #fa709a → #fee140
* #30cfd0 → #330867
* #a8edea → #fed6e3
* The content card uses rgba(255,255,255,0.95) with backdrop-filter: blur(10px), 20px border-radius, 60px padding all sides, and box-shadow: 0 20px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.3).
* Typography within the card:
* Year: 80px bold, gradient fill clipped to text using #667eea → #764ba2
* Date label: 18px, weight 600, uppercase, 2px letter-spacing, color #764ba2, 15px bottom margin
* Title: 36px bold, color #333, line-height 1.2, 20px bottom margin
* Description: 18px, color #666, line-height 1.8, 30px bottom margin
* Milestone badge: pill with #667eea → #764ba2 gradient background, white text, 14px weight 600, uppercase, 1px letter-spacing, 8px 20px padding, 20px border-radius
* The watermark number behind each card is 120px bold, color rgba(255,255,255,0.1), positioned absolute top-left 30px from each edge, z-index behind the card.
* The scroll hint badge uses rgba(255,255,255,0.2) background with backdrop-filter: blur(10px), white text 14px weight 600, 15px 25px padding, 30px border-radius.
* It pulses with an opacity animation cycling between 0.6 and 1.0 over 2s, infinite, easing in and out.
### Behaviour

* On page load, all milestone panels are created from the data array and appended to the wrapper in array order before any user interaction.
* Vertical wheel input (deltaY !== 0) is intercepted with preventDefault() on a non-passive listener ({ passive: false }) and translated 1:1 into horizontal scroll on the document body.
* The user scrolls left and right through panels without any native horizontal scroll gesture.
* The custom scrollbar remains visible at all times as a secondary navigation affordance.
* No snapping, no smooth-scroll override — the remapped scroll is immediate and linear.
* The scroll hint badge is always visible in the bottom-right corner regardless of scroll position.
* It has no dismiss or hide behaviour.
### Responsive

* There are no explicit media-query breakpoints in the original component.
* All sizing is expressed in viewport units so the layout scales continuously.
* The following adaptations should be added for narrower viewports:
* Below 768px: reduce panel horizontal padding from 100px to 24px; content card padding from 60px to 24px; year from 80px to 48px; title from 36px to 24px; description from 18px to 15px
* Below 480px: content card max-width 100% (fills between paddings); watermark number reduced from 120px to 64px
### Code Quality

* All milestone content lives exclusively in the data array.
* No milestone text, year, or gradient appears in the HTML markup — the document source contains only the structural shell (wrapper, timeline rule, scroll hint).
* The rendering function iterates the array once and produces one panel per entry; adding or removing a milestone requires only a change to the data array.
* The scroll-remapping listener and the rendering function are fully decoupled — each has a single responsibility.
* The wheel listener must be attached once to window with { passive: false } and must call preventDefault() before any scroll mutation to suppress native vertical scrolling.
* Background gradients are stored as CSS gradient strings in the data array and applied via element.style.background — they are never hardcoded into CSS rules, keeping the stylesheet free of per-panel styles.

Build a countdown timer component that displays the remaining time until a fixed target date. The timer updates every second and shows days, hours, minutes, and seconds as zero-padded two-digit numbers separated by colon dividers. An eyebrow label sits above the timer row describing the occasion.

### Dependencies
* No external dependencies.
### Architecture
* The target date is a single hardcoded Date value (2026-09-01T00:00:00).
* A self-invoking function runs one tick immediately on load then calls itself on a 1000 ms interval.
* Each tick computes the difference between the target and the current timestamp, derives days/hours/minutes/seconds via integer division and modulo against millisecond constants (86400000, 3600000, 60000, 1000), clamps to zero when the countdown expires, and writes the zero-padded values into four separate number elements by ID.
### Layout
* The outer wrapper is a centered column (flex, column direction, center-aligned) with 60px top/bottom padding and 40px left/right padding.
* The eyebrow label sits above the timer row with 32px bottom margin.
* The timer row is a flex row with 24px gap between items.
* Each unit is a centered flex column (minimum width 56px) containing a large number above a small label.
* Colon separators sit between each unit pair, vertically offset 6px from the top to optically align with the numbers.
### Styling
* All text uses proxima-nova.
* Eyebrow: 11px, letter-spacing 0.3em, uppercase.
* Numbers: 48px, font-weight 300, letter-spacing -0.02em, line-height 1.
* Labels: 9px, color #999, letter-spacing 0.2em, uppercase, 10px top margin.
* Colon separators: 36px, font-weight 300, color #ccc.
### Behaviour

A scroll-aware page navigation component that tracks which section the user is currently viewing and reflects that state through a progress line and dot indicators. On desktop it sits as a fixed vertical rail on the left edge of the viewport, centred vertically. On mobile it becomes a fixed bottom bar with a horizontal track. Both versions update in real time as the user scrolls, and each dot or label can be clicked to smooth-scroll directly to its target section.

### Dependencies

* No external dependencies.
### Architecture

* The component consists of two sibling nav elements rendered in HTML — one for desktop, one for mobile — each containing the same number of dots, a static track line, and a dynamic progress fill element.
* Each dot carries a data attribute pointing to the ID of its corresponding page section.
* On scroll, a single update function reads the current scroll position, determines the active section index (a section becomes active once the scroll position reaches 40% of the viewport height above its top edge, with the last section forced active when the bottom of the page is within 20px of the viewport bottom), then applies an active state to the matching dot in both nav variants and advances the progress fill proportionally.
* The desktop fill is driven by percentage height; the mobile fill by percentage width.
### Layout

* Desktop nav: a fixed vertical column anchored 28px from the left edge, centred vertically with transform: translateY(-50%).
* The track line and progress fill are absolutely positioned to run through the vertical centre of the dot column.
* Dots are 28x28px hit targets stacked in a column; each dot's visible pip is 7x7px centred inside it.
* Section labels sit inline to the right of each dot, appearing only on hover or when active.
* Mobile nav: a fixed bottom bar spanning the full viewport width.
* It is a column with two rows: the top row is a flex row of evenly spaced text labels; the bottom row is a flex row of evenly spaced dot buttons (24x24px) with the track line and progress fill running absolutely through their horizontal midpoint.
* The bar has 10px top padding and 16px bottom padding, with 24px horizontal padding.
* A gap of 6px separates the two rows.
### Styling

* Palette: background cream #f5f0e8, gold accent #b89a6a, gold-light border #d4b896, soft text #6d6255, rule line rgba(26,23,20,0.12).
* Desktop dot pip: 7x7px circle, 1px border in gold-light, filled with the cream background at rest.
* On hover and when active: background and border shift to gold, the pip scales up to 1.3x with a 0.2s ease transition.
* Desktop labels: 9px, weight 400, letter-spacing 0.25em, uppercase, soft text colour, hidden (opacity 0, nudged left by 6px) at rest.
* On hover or active: opacity 1, translate to natural position, over 0.2s ease.
* Desktop progress line: 1px wide, gold, height animates via transition: height 0.15s ease.
* Mobile bar: background rgba(245,240,232,0.92) with backdrop-filter: blur(12px), 1px top border in the rule colour.
* Mobile labels: 8px, weight 400, letter-spacing 0.2em, uppercase, soft text colour at rest; gold when active, with 0.2s ease colour transition.

* Scroll tracking: A passive scroll listener fires an update function on every scroll event.
* The function iterates the sections in order; a section becomes the active candidate when the page scroll position is greater than or equal to that section's top offset minus 40% of the viewport height.

* If the sum of scroll position and viewport height reaches within 20px of the full document height, the last section is forced active regardless.

* Progress fill — mobile: The fill width is calculated as activeIndex / (totalDots - 1) * 100%.
* At the first section the fill is 0%; at the last it is 100%.

### Goal
A vertically scrollable page with a year navigation bar that begins inline and locks as a fixed sticky header when scrolled past. Content sections fade in on scroll. All data is defined in a JavaScript array. No external dependencies.

### Dependencies
* No external dependencies.

### Architecture
* Data: START_YEAR and END_YEAR define the year range; year buttons and content sections are generated programmatically from these values — no hard-coded HTML per year.
* Three IntersectionObservers: (1) sentinel observer — a zero-height element immediately above the nav triggers fixed positioning when it leaves the viewport; (2) scrollspy observer — watches content sections to highlight the active year button; (3) fade observer — watches content sections to fade them in and out.
* A spacer element matches the nav bar height and is hidden by default; it becomes visible when the nav goes fixed to prevent layout jump.
* On year button click: the corresponding section scrolls into view and the year button scrolls to the center of the carousel.

### Layout
* Intro section: max-width 900px, centered.
* Year carousel: full viewport width, 64px height, horizontally scrollable (overflow-x: auto, white-space: nowrap).
* Content sections: max-width 900px, centered. White cards with 10px border-radius, min-height 260px, and a subtle box-shadow.

### Styling
* Page background: #f5f5f7. Accent color: #1a1a2e.
* Active year button: font-weight 700, color #000, background rgba(0,0,0,0.06).
* Fixed nav: gains a box-shadow to signal elevation.
* Content sections: opacity 0 and translateY 24px by default; fade to opacity 1 and translateY 0 over 0.6s ease when visible.

### Behaviour

special/ScrollZoomGrowPanHero.html:
### Goal
A scroll-driven hero section with two sequential animation phases. In the grow phase, a centred title shrinks and fades while a small image scales up from a compact size to full viewport width, anchored at the top edge so it expands downward. In the pan phase, once the image reaches full width, it pans upward to reveal the rest of a tall portrait image, like scrolling through a tall photo. A nav bar and a copy block fade in during the pan phase. Vanilla JavaScript only — no external libraries.

### Dependencies
* No external dependencies.
### Architecture
* The outer section's height is set by JavaScript once the image's natural aspect ratio is known, giving the scroll engine the exact canvas needed.
* Pin switching: instead of CSS `position: sticky` (which breaks under ancestor overflow or transform), the pin element switches programmatically between absolute → fixed → absolute. When the section top is above 0, the pin is absolute at top 0; inside the pinned range it is fixed at top 0; after the range it is absolute at the bottom of the grow+pan distance.
* Two CSS custom properties drive the image animation: `--image-scale` (grow phase) and `--image-pan` (pan phase). Three more properties control overlay opacity: `--nav-opacity`, `--copy-opacity`, and `--intro-opacity`.
* A `requestAnimationFrame` loop (passive scroll listener) updates all custom properties on each scroll tick.
* `recalcLayout()` computes grow distance (viewport height × GROW_VH_MULTIPLIER) and pan distance (image layout height − viewport height) and sets the section height. It runs on load and on resize.
### Layout
* The `.scroll-zoom-hero__pin` element is 100vh tall and positioned relative to the outer section.
* The image-wrap is absolutely positioned inset 0, aligned flex-start (top-anchored) so the image grows downward.
* The title is fixed in the viewport, centred, shifted and scaled by CSS custom properties.
* The intro block is fixed at top 10%, left 20% — it fades out early in the grow phase.
* The nav bar is absolutely positioned at the top of the pin, fades in during the pan phase.
* The copy block is absolutely positioned at bottom-right of the pin, fades in during the pan phase.
### Styling
* Pin background: var(--bg, #f4f2ee).
* Title: white, 35px, weight 600, centered, pointer-events none. Transform combines translateY(--title-shift) and scale(--title-scale).
* Image: transform-origin top center (grows downward, top edge stays fixed). Transform combines translateY(--image-pan) and scale(--image-scale).
* Nav: uppercase, 13px, letter-spacing 0.02em. Fades in and slides down via --nav-opacity.
* Copy overlay: white text, right 6%, bottom 12%, max-width 380px. Eyebrow 12px weight 600 uppercase, body 15px, link 13px uppercase.
### Behaviour
* Grow phase eased with easeOutQuad. Image scale goes from START_SCALE (default 0.68) to 1. Title scale ends at 0.45 and shifts upward to TITLE_TOP_REST_PX (100px) from the top. Intro fades out by 40% grow progress.
* Pan phase begins once grow is complete. Image pans upward by panDistance pixels. Nav fades in over the first 30% of pan progress; copy fades in between 15% and 50% of pan progress.
* Scroll listener uses { passive: true }. ticking flag prevents multiple rAF calls per frame.
* Image load event triggers recalcLayout so the section height is correct before any scrolling.
### Responsive
* No explicit breakpoint changes. The layout is driven by viewport height (vh units) and the image's natural aspect ratio, so it adapts to any screen size automatically.

special/CursorGIFTrail.html:
### Goal
A decorative cursor effect that replaces the native cursor with a trail of GIF icons that follow the mouse with a smooth chasing delay. Multiple trail elements are created, each with decreasing opacity and scale, and each chases the position of the element in front of it (not the raw mouse position directly), creating a flowing tail effect.

### Dependencies
* No external dependencies.
### Architecture
* TRAIL_COUNT (default 8) trail elements are created and appended to the body.
* Each trail element has progressively lower opacity (linear fade from 1 to near-zero) and smaller scale (using CSS transform on the element itself at creation time).
* A `trails` array stores each element and its current x/y position.
* On each `requestAnimationFrame` tick, the first trail chases the mouse position with a lerp factor of 0.3. Each subsequent trail chases the position of the element before it with the same factor.
* Each element is positioned with left/top style, offset by half the element width/height (16px) to center it on its tracked point.
### Styling
* `body { cursor: none; }` — hides the native cursor.
* `.cursor-trail`: fixed positioning, 32x32px, pointer-events none, z-index 9999, background-image: url to cursor.gif (no-repeat, center, contain).
* Opacity and transform scale are set inline at element creation time.
### Behaviour
* mousemove updates mouseX/mouseY globals.
* animate() runs in a requestAnimationFrame loop: for each trail, lerp x/y toward the target (first trail targets mouse, rest target previous trail), then set left/top style.
* No pause on mouse leave — trails settle to the last known mouse position naturally.
### Responsive
* No breakpoint changes. Fixed positioning keeps trails in viewport space at all sizes.
### Output Requirements
* Return only the component implementation — do not include <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head>, <body>, or <title>
* Output in this order: dependency CSS imports, dependency JavaScript imports, HTML, CSS, JavaScript
* Place all dependency imports at the beginning

* Use semantic HTML where appropriate
* Write clean, reusable, and modular code
* Do not use libraries other than those listed in Dependencies
special/CursorGIFFollower.html:
### Goal
A minimal decorative cursor effect that replaces the native cursor with a single GIF icon that follows the mouse in real time. Unlike the trail variant, there is no chasing delay — the GIF moves exactly with the cursor on every mousemove event.

### Dependencies
* No external dependencies.
### Architecture
* A single `.cursor-follower` div is present in the HTML.
* A mousemove listener on the document updates the element's left and top style properties to e.clientX - 16 and e.clientY - 16 (centering the 32px icon on the cursor hotspot).
### Styling
* `body { cursor: none; }` — hides the native cursor.
* `.cursor-follower`: fixed positioning, 38x38px, pointer-events none, z-index 9999, background-image: url to cursor.gif (no-repeat, center, contain).
### Behaviour
* Direct mousemove → style update, no lerp or animation frame loop.
### Responsive
* No breakpoint changes. Fixed positioning keeps the follower in viewport space at all sizes.
